newsitem.title: USA: N. Carolina may bond for bridge, rail projects.
newsitem.headline: N. Carolina may bond for bridge, rail projects.

text.p: North Carolina may issue bonds to partly finance two major bridge and rail projects, in addition to the $950 million of highway bonds approved by voters last fall, state Highway Administrator Larry Goode said Friday.

The projects include an $80 million toll bridge linking the Outer Banks to the mainland and a $400 million high-speed rail system linking Raleigh and Charlotte, Goode told the Bond Buyer Southeast Public Finance Conference in Atlanta.

The state has not built a new toll road in 40 years and its residents generally loathe even the mention of tolls, Goode said. But the state was able to establish an authority to issue toll-backed debt for the new bridge with little protest from residents because the tolls will be paid mainly by tourists.
Goode said the state would probably issue about $40 million to $50 million of revenue bonds for the project, though the timing was uncertain.
For the rail project, Goode said the state already owns 75 percent of the tracks that would be used and is negotiating to buy out the minority owners.

It has committed $15 million this year to improve rail signals and allow the trains to go faster, cutting about 20 minutes off the three-hour trip between Raleigh and Charlotte. Meeting its goal of shaving the travel time to under two hours would require additional improvmebnts that would bring the total project cost to $400 million, Goode said.
He said the state would seek federal mass transit funds to pay for part of the project and that "I think bonds will be in the mix."
The projects are the latest in a series of major transportation undertakings in North Carolina, where all highways are state-owned and run.

In November, North Carolina voters approved $950 million of general obligation bonds to build urban loops, widen two-lane highways and pave rural roads. Those bonds will be issued over two or three years.
